newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas untraded again, awaits first deal of we.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas untraded again, awaits first deal of we.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures market was untraded again on Wednesday morning, so no trade has now been done so far this week.

Although there were bids posted on all periods except August by the close of the morning session, offers were only seen on the first seven months. In the six months where both bids and offers were posted, they were placed on either side of the previous settlement level and from September onwards they were between 0.50 pence and 1.00 pence apart.
Front-month June was bid at 11.20 pence a therm by the close and offered at 11.50 pence.
The IPE has introduced changes to the Energy Trading System (ETS) to help prevent errors in entering bids and offers and to bring trading practices in line with other floor-traded markets.
A futures broker said the changes should help them in reducing errors but they were unlikely to help boost the liquidity of the contract.
